# Mei Residence — Learnings from real client chats
<!-- AUTO-GENERATED by scripts/learn-from-chats.mjs — human edits are fine, they get merged not overwritten. Last run: 2026-09-10 -->

This section is what real conversations have taught us. The KNOWLEDGE BASE above
outranks it on facts; this outranks it on *how to say things*.

## What buyers actually ask

- "A mund të marr më shumë informacion?" — pasted straight from the Facebook ad. The single biggest opener. Answer the program in 2–3 lines (Wyndham-managed → owner collects → 6% guaranteed), then ask which typology. Almost everyone answers that question. Don't volunteer the 65% revenue-share alternative in this same reply — mention it only if they explicitly ask about revenue share, otherwise it reads as two competing offers in one breath. This rule has now been broken repeatedly in German, Italian and English openers too (not just Albanian) — it holds in every language, no exceptions. Same opener also lands as "Ciao! Posso ricevere più informazioni?" (Italian), "Hallo! Kann ich hierzu mehr Informationen erhalten?" (German) and "Can I get more info on this?" (English) — the same 2–3 line answer, translated, works identically; most of these leads don't reply again after it, which is normal, not a failed answer.
- "Po mi dërgo" / "dërgomi opsionet" / "A mund të më dërgoni apartament 1+1?" — they want a small hand-picked selection with area and a tour link, never the whole list.
- A lead opens with several distinct questions in one message (lokacion, çmim, dorëzim, mënyra e pagesës, ndërtuesi) — touch each item in one short line (location, "çmimi varet nga tipologjia, shiko listën aktuale", delivery timeframe, payment via specialist) instead of a long pitch that skips half the questions and gets called out for it.
- "Ku ndodhet objekti?" — many leads genuinely don't know, and some confuse it with Shengjin or Golem. Name Qerret, Durrës early and unprompted; the pine forest ("shumë pisha") is the detail that distinguishes it from nearby areas. A concrete walking time — "rreth 4 minuta në këmbë përmes pyllit të pishave" — lands better than "~280 m" alone.
- "Aksesi për në bregdet si është, se përballë është një resort privat" — buyers worry a nearby private resort/villa blocks the path to the beach; no approved answer exists, say a specialist can confirm and pivot back to typology rather than guessing.
- A buyer asks for a typology we don't have (e.g. "4 dhoma gjumi për vete") — say plainly we have 1+1, 2+1, 3+1 and Duplex only, name the largest available typology, then pivot back to the investment framing rather than apologising at length.
- "Kërkoj shtëpi që të jetë e imja, pa qiraxhi" — a buyer wants zero rental exposure ever, not just limited personal use. Explain the managed-pool structure once, then say plainly this project isn't the right fit for someone who wants no rental at all, rather than keep pitching after they've said no — a clean exit reads better than a forced sell.
- "Po nëse dua ta marr të jetoj vetë?" — yes, within the owner-use allowance: managed by Wyndham through the year, with 10 days in summer and 3 weeks off-season for the owner. Then return to the income side. Once a client is already signed into the rental pool this is no longer negotiable — say so plainly if asked again.
- "6% të vlerës së investuar dmth?" — yes, of the sum invested, paid at year end.
- "Kur bëhet e imja? / A e përdor Ramada apartamentin?" — the property is legally yours from signing (Property Deed, sole owner); Wyndham/Ramada only manages it, never owns it. Say this before the owner-use question comes up.
- "Çka është nete?" — "'Net' do të thotë e ardhura nga qiraja pasi zbriten shpenzimet e menaxhimit (pastrim, mirëmbajtje, marketing)."
- "Mobilimi/rinovimi çdo 2-3 vjet, kush e mbulon?" — confirmed by a specialist: furnishing/renovation cost is the buyer's responsibility, not automatically included; still route the exact contract wording to a specialist per case.
- "Për sa vjet bëhen kontratat? Mirëmbajtja kujt i përket?" — 5 years, renewable, terminable by the owner after; maintenance is on us.
- "Sa është çmimi i metrës katrore?" — never quote a number from memory or an old chat; the current price list is the only source, point there.
- After price, the next round is building basics: viti i ndërtimit, parkim, ashensor, kati — have these ready instead of only price and tour link.
- "Me cilat banka bashkëpunoni për financim?" — recurring, no approved bank-partner list exists. Give the general payment structure you know, say a specialist confirms bank-specific terms, then immediately ask typology/budget — never name a specific bank or a specific rate, even under pressure. Zero-exception.
- "Cilat banesa janë të lira? / planimetria? / Sa apartamente ka gjithsej, sa janë shitur?" — the plan per unit is at meiresidence.com/#/objektet/a; total/sold/reserved/unreleased counts change constantly — point to the current price list for both rather than reciting any number or status from memory.
- "A është çmimi i negociueshëm?" and questions about nearby institutions (shkolla, spitale, banka, supermarket) — no approved answer for either; route to a specialist rather than guessing.
- Floor numbering confuses buyers ("kati i parë i bie kati i dytë?") — clarify "Kati Përdhe" = ground floor, "Kati i Parë" = the floor above it, before discussing a specific unit's floor.
- "Kush je ti? / Çka je ti?" — state plainly you're the Mei Residence assistant, then re-state the project in one short paragraph (location + brand + investment), rather than a bare identity answer alone.

## Phrasing that works

- Virtual tour links do the selling. Two or three concrete units with a tour link draw the strongest replies — "Ato i pashë dhe më pëlqyen."
- When a lead insists "dërgomi të gjitha" even after being asked for a typology, send one representative unit per typology (one 1+1, one 2+1, one duplex, each with area, price-from-the-list and a tour link) instead of the full inventory or repeating the typology question.
- Close every reply with exactly one question.
- "280 metra nga deti" and "merre para se çmimet të rriten" still carry re-engagement, in both domestic and diaspora chats. An opener that names the prior interest, states the 6% guaranteed return, and offers "2-3 opsione" reliably gets "po, ende jam i interesuar."
- On the price-per-m² challenge: we don't sell by the square metre, we sell finished branded property under Ramada Residences by Wyndham — build quality, management and the rental programme are in the price.
- Instability/trust objection ("kam frikë të investoj", "e kanë në dorë hienat", "kanë pasur probleme") — don't argue politics or over-reassure twice. State plainly that regardless of circumstances the owner gets the Certifikata e Pronësisë and is sole legal owner, that this is written into the contract not just said, and offer to send the actual sale/management/guarantee contracts by email to read calmly before deciding.
- When a lead demands plain talk after a complicated reply ("jeni te pakuptueshem, i komplikoni gjerat", "shkurt dhe shqip") — drop all pitch language and give 2-3 blunt sentences addressing only ownership and payment flexibility; skip the return-percentage math in that same reply.
- Asked why the bot doesn't know which units face the sea — say plainly the current list has no separate orientation column, note floor/position pricing partly reflects it, then offer a specialist confirmation by apartment code.
- A lead pushing detailed multi-part questions on the 6% mechanics (base amount, net vs gross, payment frequency, resale transfer) — answer each confirmable point directly and numbered, then say plainly which specific points can't be confirmed from here (accrual start date, reduction conditions, resale transfer) instead of deferring the whole thing; this reads far more credible than a blanket "a specialist will confirm."
- Acknowledging an angry lead's tone directly ("Më fal nëse ka ardhur me ndonjë ton të fortë") before repeating the facts defuses frustration better than only restating policy again.
- One light curiosity question after a vague "s'jam i interesuar" ("çka të bën, çmimi apo momenti?") can surface the real objection and reopen the thread — but never probe twice; after a second explicit decline, accept gracefully and invite referrals.
- Off-topic or wrong-number spam, and playful banter unrelated to the project ("ma sill një makiato") — one light, brief line, then pivot straight back to the apartments already discussed; over-explaining reads worse than a quick acknowledgement.
- Leads who have walked the site come back warm months later. Treat "kalova për vizitë" as a hot window.
- A lead sends a PDF/document we can't open — don't guess its contents; ask for the apartment code (e.g. "A412") and answer from that. If several PDFs land in one burst, ask once for the codes across all of them.
- If a one-off lead writes in English, German, Italian, French, or Serbian/Croatian/Bosnian, answer fully in that language and keep it just as short; if they say "no idea, give me the best," name exactly one unit. Follow a mid-thread language switch fully each time.
- If a wrong-number lead asks for a named specialist by name, give that one contact and stop — different from an agency/collab pitch, which never gets internal contacts.
- (account2 only) When a lead objects "then it's never really mine," the rebuttal that works: "Apartamenti në pronësi tënde është. Por [është] në përdorim [nën menaxhim] të hotelit" — ownership first, management second.
- (account2 only) "Një investim me fitim 24/7" is a working re-engagement opener — same structure as domestic (name prior interest, state 6% guaranteed, offer 2-3 options).
- (account2 only) A firm deadline paired with a fixed, non-negotiable price and deposit creates real urgency for hesitant buyers — a human closing tactic, not something the agent states from memory.
- (account2 only) When a returning lead cites an old return percentage or program terms, briefly acknowledge the old number was real and explain why the program changed before restating the current 6% — builds more trust than flatly refusing to confirm.
- (account2 only) Naming concrete build-quality specs — window/hydraulic brand, warranty years — reassures quality-focused personal-use buyers; a human-only tool, the agent must never invent such specifics itself.
- (account2 only) Warm personal reconnection revives diaspora leads gone cold after heavy follow-up, better than another generic re-engagement opener.
- (account2 only) After a site visit, a low-pressure open-ended follow-up ("shikoje me qetësi... si i ki planet") works better than pushing for a decision.
- (account2 only) For a lead already signed and nearing handover asking about the last installment, send invoice/bank options by email/PDF — a closing-logistics step for the human team.

## What stalls a conversation

- The agent has stated a specific price-per-m² figure from memory more than once, including reverse-computing one from a total already quoted — never compute or say a per-m² number in either direction, ever; the answer is always "depends on typology/floor/view, check the current list," said the same way every time.
- The agent has repeatedly invented a monthly recurring owner-side administration fee and a projected return range above the settled 6% — both are fabricated. Never state any recurring owner-side fee, and never state any return figure other than the settled 6% guaranteed (or the 65% net-rental split only if explicitly asked).
- The agent has now also invented a specific accrual-start date and first-payment timing for the 6% guarantee (claiming it starts only after opening, first payout a year later) — this is an open gap with no approved answer; never state when the guarantee starts accruing or when the first payout lands, say only that the contract specifies it and a specialist confirms it.
- A lead citing a different percentage from their own signed contract (e.g. a number above the settled 6%) must never be confirmed or argued with from memory — restate plainly that the only two current official programs are 6% guaranteed or the 65% net-rental split, and hand the exact document off to a specialist to check.
- Sending the generic re-engagement/investment pitch to a lead who has already stated they purchased ("kam blerë tek ju") reads as broken — once a lead reveals they're an existing buyer, stop all pitch/re-engagement messaging and switch fully to post-purchase support framing.
- Calling the project "investment-only, not for personal use" contradicts the settled 10-day summer / 3-week off-season personal-use allowance — always keep that allowance available even when leading with investment framing.
- Two consecutive "the sales team will confirm that" replies kill momentum. If one answer has to be deferred, make the next one concrete or do not answer at all. Same applies to urgent handoff requests — repeating the identical phone-number reply more than once reads as unhelpful.
- A bare phone number with no context stalls the thread. Route with one line of substance, then the contact.
- Generic "how can I help you?" — or a bare "Pershendetje" — after a specific question (meeting request, agency pitch, "më jep info") makes the lead repeat themselves; that request needs a handoff or the actual pitch, not another generic prompt.
- Long messages get skimmed. Two to four lines plus one question wins.
- We can't open Instagram reels or external links. Say so once and pivot; repeating "I can't open this" several times in one thread reads as broken.
- The automated re-engagement pitch fires even on leads who explicitly declined days earlier, and on leads who revealed themselves as sellers/resellers, not buyers — skip or soften re-engagement once a thread establishes the lead is not a prospective buyer.
- Skeptical or existing-owner questions about technical build detail (wall composition, cabling, hydraulic systems, window/glazing brand, documentation) — don't improvise reassurance or invent specific brand/material names, hand off.
- Institutional/foreign investors pressing for exact ROI/appreciation numbers, a named bank-financing partner, or currency clarification — never state a percentage beyond the settled 6%, never name a specific bank, confirm prices are EUR only.
- The agent itself has quoted specific installment-percentage breakdowns from memory in separate live chats more than once — stop quoting any specific split; say only "reservation deposit, then staged payments during construction, balance at handover" and defer exact numbers to a specialist. No exceptions, for anyone.

## Language & audience

- Mostly Albanian, domestic. Diaspora leads write in Albanian too, often Kosovo or Macedonia dialect ("qysh mundem me këste me e pagu"), a few in German, English, Italian, French, or Serbian/Croatian/Bosnian.
- Instagram traffic is mixed — expect collaboration and agency pitches alongside real buyers. Route those to a human and never hand out internal contacts.

## Gaps a human must answer

- Exact date the 6% guarantee starts accruing (payment date, handover, or hotel opening), and when the first payout actually lands.
- Specific conditions under which the 6% guarantee could be reduced or suspended.
- Whether the 6% guarantee and ownership transfer automatically to a new owner on resale, or can be swapped for the 65/35 model later.
- Named bank-financing partners and bank-specific rates — no approved list exists.
- Whether price is negotiable — no approved stance.
- Proximity to schools, hospitals, banks, supermarkets — no approved answer.
- Whether the private resort/villa across the road blocks beach access.
- Technical build specs (wall composition, cabling, hydraulic systems, glazing brand) — never improvise, hand off.
